title: Construction Sales Funnel: Win Contracts at Better Margins
meta_description: A sales funnel for construction company owners turning over £1M+: qualify better leads, win more contracts, and build a pipeline that scales.
h1: Construction Sales Funnel: Win Contracts at Better Margins
hero_subtitle: A practical guide to turning the right enquiries into signed contracts at margins worth having.

intro.answer: Most construction businesses at £1M turnover are not short of enquiries. They are short of the right enquiries, at the right margin, from clients worth keeping. That is what a sales funnel actually solves.

image.alt: Construction sales funnel stages from first enquiry through to signed contract

intro.roadmap: This guide covers how to build and run that funnel from first contact through to repeat business, using the Plan, Attract, Convert, Deliver and Scale framework built for UK construction businesses scaling toward £5M. Whether you have never thought about your sales process systematically, or you are already doing parts of this and seeing gaps, the same five stages apply.

briefing.title: Qualify Before You Quote, Then Track Four Numbers
briefing.intro: Qualification and follow-up give the fastest visible return of anything in this guide, so they are worth doing before you change anything else. At £1M+ turnover a detailed quote can take four to eight hours of estimating time, plus site visits and supplier pricing. Spending that on someone who was never serious is a direct and measurable cost.

panels.heading: How do you qualify a construction enquiry before quoting?
paragraphs: Not every enquiry deserves a full priced tender. Before you commit estimating time, find out the project scope and expected start date, their budget expectation, whether they have worked with a contractor before and what happened, whether they are the person who signs the contract, and why they contacted you specifically.
If their budget is half of what the job realistically costs, or they are vague on every detail, walk away early. That estimating time is worth more on a lead that fits your criteria.

panels.heading: Track the route from enquiry to signed contract
paragraphs: You cannot improve what you do not measure. Track these four every month and the funnel will tell you where to focus.
steps: Enquiries in. How many new leads entered the funnel this month?
Decided-quote win rate. Compare similar projects and periods; report pending quotes separately.
Average project value. Is it growing year on year, or are you winning the same size jobs?
Time to close. Compare similar project types and the decision timetable agreed with each buyer.

review.label: Review monthly
review.text: Pick the weakest link in your funnel and fix that one first. Trying to overhaul every stage at once is how the whole thing stalls.

brief_before_heading: Plan: Know Exactly Who You’re Targeting

append_sections.heading: What should a builder say when following up a quote?
paragraphs: Follow-up should reduce uncertainty, not create pressure. Ask about the decision process and any blocker. Avoid false urgency or invented deadlines.

Receipt and clarification: Hi, did the proposal for your project come through clearly? Are there any questions about the scope, timing or payment stages? Would a short call help, and when are you expecting to make a decision?

Agreed decision date: Hi, we agreed to check in today about your project. Has the decision timetable changed, or is there anything you need us to clarify? If the project is on hold, let me know whether and when you would like us to contact you again.
steps: Use the templates as starting points and adapt the tone to the client.
Ask about the decision process, the blocker and the next action.
Offer to clarify scope, programme or terms without pressure.
Record the reply, agreed next action, date and owner.
append_sections.before_heading: Deliver: Turn Every Project Into Your Next Contract

append_sections.heading: When should you stop chasing a building quote?
paragraphs: Stop when the buyer asks you to stop. Respect contact permissions and preferences. Otherwise, work from an agreed next action, date and owner. A promised decision date is more useful than a universal interval. If no date is promised, agree one or pause.

Separate paused from lost. Paused means timing, scope or budget is not ready, but future contact is welcome. Lost means no fit, another choice or a clear no. Scheduled tenders follow the buyer's rules and deadlines, not normal quote follow-up.

For quotes issued in the same period, calculate decided-quote win rate as wins divided by wins plus losses, multiplied by 100. Show paused and still-pending quotes separately. If none has reached a decision, report the rate as not yet available. Compare similar job types and allow time for larger projects to decide.

text_replacements.find: Research consistently shows that over 80% of sales require five or more follow-up contacts before a decision is made. In construction, a client might be sitting on three quotes while they finalise planning permission, secure funding, or wait for a board sign-off. The contractor who stays in contact professionally, without being pushy, is almost always the one who wins when the client is ready to move.
text_replacements.replace: A client may be comparing proposals while waiting for drawings, funding or an internal decision. Agree when to reconnect and use each conversation to clarify the next step. Follow-up cannot guarantee a win.

text_replacements.find: Your website is the single most valuable lead-generation asset you own. For most construction businesses at this level, 60 to 70% of inbound enquiries start with a Google search. Yet most construction websites are thin on substance: no case studies, no clear offer, no social proof, and no obvious reason to get in touch.
text_replacements.replace: Your website should help a suitable prospect assess your work. Show relevant projects, a clear offer, credible proof and a straightforward way to enquire. Track your own lead sources before deciding where to invest.

text_replacements.find: Architects, structural engineers, quantity surveyors, planning consultants: these professionals refer work to contractors constantly. One solid relationship with a well-connected architect can be worth £150,000 to £250,000 a year in project flow. You don’t need dozens of these relationships. You need to be the contractor they call first when the right opportunity comes up.
text_replacements.replace: Architects, engineers and quantity surveyors can introduce suitable work when they understand your capabilities. Build relationships around relevant completed projects and reliable delivery. See how to attract the right construction clients and assess higher-value opportunities.

text_replacements.find: The average satisfied construction client personally knows two or three other potential clients. Your funnel doesn’t just run forward; it loops back and compounds over time.
text_replacements.replace: Ask satisfied clients whether they would be comfortable making a relevant introduction. Record referrals and the work they produce rather than assuming every client will bring another project.
